 Neon's pricing is built for this pattern. Each tenant gets its own project, an isolated Postgres database with its own compute, and there's no per-project or per-database fee:

  + Free plan: up to 100 projects at $0, each with its own 100 CU-hours and 1 GB of storage, enough to build and test a database-per-tenant app.
  + Launch and Scale: you pay only for the compute each tenant actually runs and the storage it holds. Idle tenant databases scale to zero, so inactive tenants don't add compute cost; storage is still billed. Launch includes 100 projects, and Scale includes 1,000, with more on request. [...] For example, if your databases are mostly idle that month, or you only run them briefly for development or testing, you'll only pay for the compute and storage actually consumed during that time. Remember that Neon databases scale to zero by default.
 No. When you're on a paid plan, database usage starts metering from zero for both compute and storage. Free plan quotas don't apply once you upgrade. Instead, you're billed purely based on actual usage, at the rates of your paid plan.

  You should consider a paid plan if:

  + You expect higher or more sustained usage than what's included per project on the Free plan
  + You care about production guarantees, such as consistent availability, predictable performance, and never having your database paused due to usage limits [...] For example, 100 tenant databases on Launch, each running at 0.25 CU for about an hour a day and storing 150 MB, use about 750 CU-hours and 15 GB of storage: roughly $85 a month in total, or about $0.85 per tenant.

  Platforms that provision databases for their users at scale can apply to the Agent Plan. For design guidance, see Multitenancy with Neon.
 Neon's paid plans don't require a minimum monthly spend or base fee. You're billed purely based on usage. If one month you barely use Neon, your bill might be just a few dollars.

# Neon Pricing in 2026: Plans, Costs, and Limits Explained

Written by Denis Kildishev Denis Kildishev

  Neon Pricing in 2026: Plans, Costs, and Limits Explained 

Neon pricing starts with a free plan; paid Launch and Scale plans charge for actual usage with no monthly minimum. Database compute costs $0.106 per CU-hour on Launch and $0.222 on Scale, with storage billed separately. The main budget question is how much compute runs, and for how long—not how many colleagues log in.

Pricing checked September 25, 2026. US dollars; taxes excluded from illustrative calculations. Annual rates are monthly equivalents, not monthly invoices.

## Neon pricing at a glance [...] Neon Free, Launch, and Scale pricing; usage rates and example spend. Captured September 25, 2026. Official source.

## What each plan includes

### Free: validate the workload first

Free provides 100 projects and scales an individual compute up to 2 CU. Its database storage and compute allowances apply per project. That makes it useful for development, but a database that fits today can exceed the storage allowance as application records accumulate. Free compute suspends after five minutes of inactivity.

### Launch: pay for resources as the app grows

### Pricing

Neon is usage-based. There is a permanent free tier (0.5 GB storage and 100 compute-hours per project per month), and the Launch and Scale plans have no monthly minimum. Compute is billed per CU-hour (a CU is roughly 1 vCPU + 4 GB RAM): $0.106/CU-hour on Launch and $0.222/CU-hour on Scale. Storage is billed separately at $0.35/GB-month. The gotcha is that compute is only free while scaled to zero — an always-on database runs the compute meter around the clock. After the Databricks acquisition, storage was cut to $0.35/GB-month, compute rates dropped 15–25%, and the Scale plan gained SOC 2 Type 2 and HIPAA eligibility.

## Neon Pricing

### Plans

Neon is usage-based: you pay separately for compute (billed per CU-hour) and storage (billed per GB-month). Compute autoscales and scales to zero when idle, so an idle database costs almost nothing. Launch and Scale have no monthly minimum and no fixed base fee — the gotcha is that an always-on database that never scales to zero runs the compute meter 24/7. After Databricks acquired Neon (2025), storage was cut to $0.35/GB-month and compute rates dropped 15–25%.

### Free

## Frequently Asked Questions about Neon

Neon starts free, and the Launch and Scale plans have no monthly minimum — you pay only for usage. The part people miss is that there are two meters: compute at $0.106/CU-hour on Launch ($0.222 on Scale) and storage at $0.35/GB-month. A small app that scales to zero is nearly free; an always-on database runs the compute meter 24/7.

Neon Free gives you 0.5 GB of storage and 100 compute-hours per project per month, across up to 100 projects with 10 branches each. The limits that matter are storage size, the monthly compute-hour cap, autoscaling capped at 2 CU, and only a 6-hour point-in-time restore window.

Startup staging, business-hours use: about $20 to $36/month. A database active through the working day, idle at night and on weekends. Run 2 CU for 8 hours across 20 days (320 CU-hours × $0.106 = $33.92) plus 10 GB of storage ($3.50), and you are at roughly $36.

Always-on production: about $345 to $683/month. A 4 vCPU / 16 GB database (4 CU) that never sleeps runs 730 hours a month. On Launch, that is 2,920 CU-hours × $0.106 = $309.52, plus 100 GB of storage ($35), or about $345.

The exact same database on Scale ($0.222/CU-hour) costs about $683. Neon’s own pricing page lands in the same range: it quotes a typical spend of $701 a month on Scale for a high-load, 100 GB database, and $15 a month on Launch for an intermittent 1 GB one. [...] ## Key Takeaways

 The model in one line: Neon is usage-based serverless Postgres. You pay separately for compute (by the CU-hour), storage, branching, and backups. There is no fixed instance fee.
 The 2026 rates: compute is $0.106/CU-hour on Launch and $0.222/CU-hour on Scale, storage is $0.35/GB-month, and there has been no monthly minimum since December 2025 (use $3, pay $3).
 Cheap when idle, costly when not: a scale-to-zero side project can cost a few dollars a month, while a 24/7 production database can run into the hundreds. Same database, very different bill.
 The unit to know: 1 CU (Compute Unit) = 1 vCPU + 4 GB RAM.
 The free tier: 100 CU-hours of compute and 1 GB of storage per project, on up to 100 projects, with no credit card and no time limit. [...] ## Frequently Asked Questions

### Is Neon free?

Yes. Neon’s free tier gives every project 100 CU-hours of compute and 1 GB of storage with no credit card, and it is permanent rather than a trial. It suits prototypes and learning, but the limits are hard cutoffs and scale-to-zero cannot be disabled, so it is not built for production traffic.

### How much does Neon cost per month?

Anywhere from about $3 for an idle side project to several hundred dollars for an always-on production database. A typical startup staging setup runs $20 to $36, while a 4 CU database running 24/7 with 100 GB of storage is roughly $345 on Launch or $683 on Scale. See how that compares across providers.
